ns2:section.sectionText: Description: This course explores the origins and impacts of what historians have termed, “The Rights Revolution.” It encompasses court cases, state and federal legislation, and the changing efforts to enact legal change on everyday people, particularly those relegated to the margins of U.S. society. The course content skips across times and topics: Fourteenth Amendment, Segregation, Voting Restriction, State Anti-Discrimination, and Housing Policy. In addition to racism we look at intersections of sexism, homophobia, ablism, and xenophobia. We consider the context and dynamics of society in the post-Civil War era, World War II, the Cold War, as well as the social movements of black, women’s, and gay rights, and recent legal developments involving anti-immigration and social violence. The course assumes that participants have a strong background in historical studies and that all will commit to joining most class discussions and completing all readings and writing assignments.
